A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bulk samples are not necessarily superior to targeted samples for quantifying predation on bivalve prey, especially when data from both types of samples are standardized by shell length.
taxon-specific sampling is an excellent method for studying predation on large, abundant, and/or rare taxa, and that bulk sampling is an appropriate method for studying small, common taxa.

bulk sampling is a useful method for studying predation in bivalves when the goal is to determine the overall level of predation, but that it is less useful when the goal is a detailed understanding of the prey and predator taxa involved, the size selectivity of the predation, or the effectiveness of the prey.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the experience of the collector is more important than the type of sample collected.
taxon-specific sampling can be as effective as bulk sampling in providing quantitative data for drilling predation studies, and it can be used to obtain data on rare and large-bodied taxa.
